papers.authors: Muji Setiyo, Ilham Habibi, Saifudin, Nasmi Herlina Sari, Aditya Kolakoti
papers.summary: This paper presents a systematic review of 88 Scopus-indexed research articles published between 2021 and 2026 on the use of nanocomposites for lightweight automotive materials, detailing dominant matrix types, reinforcements, fabrication routes, mechanical property changes, emerging trends, and open challenges.
papers.methods: A systematic review of 88 Scopus-indexed research articles published between 2021 and 2026.
papers.results: Polymer matrix nanocomposites dominate the field (51.1%), followed by aluminum (30.7%) and magnesium matrices (12.5%). Graphene/derivatives and carbon nanotubes are the most frequent reinforcements. Only 5.7% of articles reported specific properties (strength or stiffness per unit mass), and most results are limited to laboratory specimens.
papers.limitations: Only 5.7% of articles reported specific properties per unit mass, most results were obtained on laboratory specimens (TRL 3-4), gains are bounded by optimum filler content causing agglomeration, and main challenges include nanoparticle dispersion, wettability, large-scale production, recycling, and lack of validation on real vehicle components.

papers.title: Geometric Reaction Path Alignment for Kinetic Feasibility Assessment
papers.authors: Nicholas Casetti, Connor W. Coley
papers.summary: The paper introduces SPARTA (Steric Path Alignment for Reactive Transformation Assessment), a geometric kinetic proxy designed to assess the kinetic feasibility of reaction paths by generating reaction-biased endpoint conformers, optimizing paths using an iterative image-dependent pair potential, and evaluating single-point energies.
papers.methods: The method generates reaction-biased endpoint conformers, refines them through iterative image-dependent pair potential path optimization, and evaluates electronic single-point energies along the resulting path. It is tested on two large reaction-barrier datasets, curated reaction classes, and applied to glucose pyrolysis and formose reaction networks.
papers.results: SPARTA barriers discriminate high- and low-barrier reactions better than reaction energy alone. It reproduces steric trends where kinetics are governed by accessibility, and successfully filters the number of candidate transition-state searches in glucose pyrolysis and formose reaction networks while retaining low-barrier reactions.
papers.limitations: Identifies clear limitations for stereoelectronically or orbital-symmetry-controlled transformations.
papers.keywords: SPARTA, reaction path alignment, kinetic feasibility, thermodynamic screening, transition-state searches, reaction networks

papers.title: Differentiable Schwarz-Coupled Solvers for Thin Boundary Layer Transport: Inverse Modeling via Agentic AI Optimization
papers.authors: Siva Viknesh, Amirhossein Arzani
papers.summary: The paper develops an overlapping Schwarz domain-decomposition framework based on perturbation theory for high-Péclet-number transport problems with thin boundary layers. It integrates differentiable physics solvers with agentic AI optimization and large language models (LLMs) to perform inverse modeling where governing equations are imposed as hard constraints.
papers.methods: An overlapping Schwarz domain-decomposition framework grounded in perturbation theory using an inner equation for near-wall dynamics and an outer equation for bulk transport, discretized using the finite element method. A fully differentiable multidomain physics solver is assembled, and large language models (LLMs) / agentic AI are integrated into the inverse workflow to propose parameter updates and grow a library of candidate basis functions during optimization.
papers.results: The formulation permits coarser mesh resolutions and reduces computational cost relative to a single-domain formulation. The agentic AI configuration is shown to be most advantageous when the spatially varying unknown is represented in a functional basis, with the AI agent growing the library of candidate basis functions in stages and initializing their parameters.

papers.authors: Krishan Chand, Ahmad Peyvan, Haoxiang Luo
papers.summary: The paper investigates the influence of non-dimensionalization on the trainability and accuracy of physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) applied to buoyancy-driven flows, using a differentially heated square cavity.
papers.methods: The study uses a differentially heated square cavity at Pr = 0.71 and Ra = 10^3–10^5 to compare thermal-diffusive and free-fall velocity scalings under identical training conditions, and performs direct gradient measurements to analyze coefficient-induced gradient imbalances.
papers.results: The free-fall scaling achieves errors below 1.1% in the mean Nusselt number for Ra <= 10^4, whereas the diffusive scaling produces errors of 157–650% and diverges at Ra = 10^5 due to a coefficient-induced gradient imbalance scaling as (Ra*Pr)^2. Sparse-data supervision and adaptive loss weighting do not resolve the training difficulties, and for unsteady convection, the free-fall PINN fails to capture the transient Nusselt-number overshoot.
papers.limitations: Tested specifically for buoyancy-driven flows in a differentially heated square cavity under certain Rayleigh and Prandtl numbers; sparse-data supervision and adaptive loss weighting failed to resolve training difficulties under the tested conditions.
papers.keywords: physics-informed neural networks (PINNs), buoyancy-driven flow, non-dimensionalization, gradient imbalance, heat transfer

papers.summary: This paper numerically investigates laminar mixed convection of MgO-water and TiO2-water nanofluids in lid-driven rectangular cavities with varying aspect ratios at a constant Reynolds number, analyzing heat transfer, flow structure, and thermal efficiency.

papers.summary: This thesis investigates a hybrid framework combining MARUS-simulated maneuvering data, Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs), and Large Language Model (LLM)-guided symbolic discovery to estimate ship maneuvering hydrodynamic derivatives for autonomous vessels, aiming to improve robustness, data efficiency, and interpretability compared to conventional methods.
papers.methods: The study uses a hybrid MARUS-PINN framework with LLM-guided symbolic discovery, utilizing Marine Robotics Unity Simulator (MARUS) data, PINN-based parameter learning, and experiments/ablation studies comparing the hybrid model with purely data-driven and purely physics-based counterparts across various USVs.
papers.results: Integrating symbolic discovery with PINNs reduces sway-acceleration error by 86%, yaw-rate acceleration error by 66%, and heading-rollout error by 89% relative to purely data-driven baselines, producing compact, physically consistent residual terms, while physics-only counterparts catastrophically diverge from ground-truths.
papers.keywords: Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs), ship maneuvering, hydrodynamic derivatives, symbolic discovery, Large Language Models (LLMs), computational fluid dynamics (CFD)
